summary:
R4 is the story right now, full stop. It's outhitting the field across every window — 66% (+11.0u) over 7 days, 62% (+18.0u) over 14, and a scorching 63% (+32.0u) since inception at n=120. Its bullpen cell is hot too, flipping to 57% over the last 14 days (99-92 aggregate territory but R4-specific 108-83) with a 3-game win streak, a real divergence from R1/R2/R3 bullpen readings sitting flat at 52%. Meanwhile the SP category is the engine for all four ratings — R1 and R2 both riding 6-game win streaks at 57% over the last 14 (109-82), and R4's season SP number leads the pack at 57% (154-116). That SP strength lines up cleanly with today's board: four of five games carry starting pitching narratives worth weighting, and the trends+sp combo remains the best-performing pair on the board at 56.8% (303-230) season-long.

On tonight's slate, all four ratings are in lockstep on every game — full consensus, no split decisions, which is the situation to lean hardest into given how R4 has been printing. The strongest number is COL @ NYY, where the delta clears +2.4 across every rating (R2 tops out at +2.75) and Fried draws a soft Rockies lineup — bet this one with confidence. TBR @ ATL is the inverse signal: every rating fades Tampa Bay on the road (R2 -1.98, the deepest number on the slate), which is notable since BOS and TBR have otherwise been the model's best "when-liked" teams (TBR 69% n=48, strong 72% +18.0u) — today the model likes ATL instead, so don't let team-loyalty bias override the number. TEX @ SEA is a similar fade of Texas (-1.18 to -1.35 across the board) despite deGrom on the mound, arguing the offense/bullpen delta is overriding the starter name value. HOU @ PHI and PIT @ CHW are both lower-conviction (deltas under 1.25), fine plays but not table-setters — treat them as secondary rather than primary units today.
